orientation: This pull request implements the Loans module for PR-7, allowing customers to apply for fixed-rate loans with monthly annuity payments and requiring loan officers to independently review, approve, or reject loan applications under four-eyes control. When approved, loan principal is disbursed to the customer's account from the bank's loan funding account in the matching currency via the ledger. The PR also includes entity persistence, module wiring, controller endpoints, and xUnit test coverage.

findings.title: Missing four-eyes check in LoanService.ApproveAsync
findings.claim: ApproveAsync does not verify whether the approving officer is also the applicant (loan.CustomerId == officerId). This allows loan officers to approve their own loans and disburse funds to themselves, violating the four-eyes requirement and causing test failure.
findings.requirement_link: POST api/loans/{id}/approve (Policies.LoanOfficer) calls ILoanService.ApproveAsync, which throws KeyNotFoundException if not found, UnauthorizedAccessException if the caller is not in Roles.LoanOfficer or if caller UserId equals Loan.CustomerId (four-eyes check), and InvalidOperationException if Loan.Status is not Submitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `if (loan.CustomerId == officerId) throw new UnauthorizedAccessException("Loan officers cannot approve their own loan.");` immediately after loading the loan.

findings.title: Class-level Customer policy blocks LoanOfficer access to Approve and Reject endpoints
findings.claim: In ASP.NET Core, authorization attributes combine additively. Placing [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] on the controller class forces all actions—including Approve and Reject—to require both Policies.Customer and Policies.LoanOfficer. Loan officers without the Customer role will receive 403 Forbidden, violating the API specification.
findings.evidence:
[ApiController]
[Route("api/loans")]
[Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)]
public sealed class LoansController : ControllerBase
findings.requirement_link: POST api/loans/{id}/approve (Policies.LoanOfficer) calls ILoanService.ApproveAsync, which throws KeyNotFoundException if not found, UnauthorizedAccessException if the caller is not in Roles.LoanOfficer or if caller UserId equals Loan.CustomerId (four-eyes check), and InvalidOperationException if Loan.Status is not Submitted.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the LoansController class and apply it directly to Apply and Get actions so Approve and Reject only require Policies.LoanOfficer.
findings.drop_reason: Capped at Major: a architecture finding is never Critical on its own

findings.title: Static LoanLocks creates an unbounded memory leak and ineffective distributed synchronization
findings.claim: LoanService stores SemaphoreSlim instances in a static ConcurrentDictionary keyed by loanId without any cleanup or eviction, leaking memory over the lifetime of the process. In-memory semaphores also fail to prevent concurrency races across multiple service instances in a distributed deployment.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> LoanLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the in-memory SemaphoreSlim dictionary and rely on database transactions and status checks (or a distributed lock if multi-node serialization is required).
anchor: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> LoanLocks = new();

findings.title: Class-level Customer policy on LoansController restricts LoanOfficer endpoints
findings.claim: LoansController is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] at the class level. In ASP.NET Core, class-level and action-level authorization attributes combine, requiring callers of Approve and Reject to satisfy both Policies.Customer and Policies.LoanOfficer, which denies loan officers who do not also possess the Customer role.

findings.suggested_fix: Remove [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)] from the controller class and place it specifically on the Apply and Get action methods.

findings.title: Unbounded memory retention in static LoanLocks dictionary
findings.claim: LoanLocks accumulates a SemaphoreSlim instance for every approved or rejected loan ID in a static ConcurrentDictionary without eviction or disposal. In a running service, this creates an unbounded memory leak as loan volume increases over time.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> LoanLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Use database row-level locking or an entity concurrency token instead of an unbounded in-memory static semaphore dictionary, or remove keys when work completes.
anchor: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> LoanLocks = new();

findings.title: Unbounded static dictionary for per-loan locks creates memory leak
findings.claim: LoanLocks statically retains a SemaphoreSlim instance for every processed loanId without eviction or cleanup. In long-running service instances, this causes monotonically increasing memory consumption.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, SemaphoreSlim> LoanLocks = new();
findings.requirement_link: Double disbursement race condition: concurrent approval requests could disburse principal multiple times if the Submitted status transition and persistence are not atomic.
findings.suggested_fix: Rely on database transactions with concurrency tokens/optimistic concurrency on the Loan entity, or remove entries from LoanLocks when locks are no longer in use.

findings.title: Annuity rounding test does not test midpoint rounding half-away-from-zero
findings.claim: The test Apply_accepts_inclusive_boundaries_and_rounds_annuity_away_from_zero claims to verify that payments round half-away-from-zero, but none of the test cases calculate a monthly payment ending in a half-cent midpoint (.XX5). For the inputs tested (169.3496..., 858.374..., 542.628...), MidpointRounding.ToEven and MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero produce identical results, so the test would pass even if banker's rounding or default rounding were used.
findings.evidence:
[Theory]
    [InlineData(1000, 6, 169.35)]
    [InlineData(10000, 12, 858.37)]
    [InlineData(50000, 120, 542.63)]
    public async Task Apply_accepts_inclusive_boundaries_and_rounds_annuity_away_from_zero(
        decimal principal, int termMonths, decimal expectedMonthlyPayment)
findings.requirement_link: ILoanService.ApplyAsync sets AnnualRatePercent to 5.5m and calculates MonthlyPayment using the standard monthly annuity formula P * r / (1 - (1 + r)^(-n)) with monthly rate r = 0.055m / 12m, rounded to 2 decimal places using Math.Round(value, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test case with principal and term values where the third decimal digit of the calculated annuity is exactly 5, ensuring that AwayFromZero rounding behaves differently from default ToEven rounding.

refusals.topic: Distributed concurrency safety across multiple API instances
refusals.reason: LoanService uses an in-memory ConcurrentDictionary with SemaphoreSlim for concurrency locking. Whether single-instance or multi-node deployment guarantees are expected for double-disbursement prevention cannot be determined from the shown context.

The test suite only includes unit tests calling LoanService directly; there are no WebApplicationFactory or integration tests verifying ASP.NET Core authorization middleware handling of the controller attributes.

refusals.topic: Distributed race condition handling across multiple service replicas
refusals.reason: In-process SemaphoreSlim only serializes concurrent calls within a single process. Whether multi-node deployments rely on database row locking or distributed locks cannot be determined without cluster deployment configuration and database isolation level settings.
